site.title: KEX-bench
site.tagline: Evaluating Coding Agents on Kernel Exploit Generation
site.description: KEX-bench evaluates whether AI agents can turn real Linux and Windows kernel vulnerabilities into verifier-confirmed exploit primitives.
site.author: KEX-bench

section_description: KEX-bench evaluates coding agents on exploit primitive generation against real Linux and Windows kernels. The benchmark contains 45 task instances across 40 CVEs, with deterministic, primitive-specific verification.

targets.name: overall
targets.description: Overall aggregates 25 Linux and 20 Windows task instances. Split bars show each platform’s contribution to the overall success rate.

targets.name: linux
targets.description: Linux includes 25 tasks across 20 CVEs: 9 kernel address leaks, 6 instruction-pointer control tasks, 6 heap reads, and 4 heap writes.

targets.name: windows
targets.description: Windows includes 20 arbitrary-address-write tasks across 20 CVEs, checked through debugger-backed memory inspection.

info_sections.title: News
info_sections.content: • EMNLP 2026 Main: “Evaluating Coding Agents on Kernel Exploit Generation” has been accepted for an oral presentation.

info_sections.title: Overview
info_sections.content: KEX-bench measures whether coding agents can construct exploit primitives against real operating-system kernels. Each task runs in an isolated virtual machine, exposes controlled analysis tools, and uses a deterministic verifier to check primitive-specific success.

info_sections.title: Evaluation Settings
info_sections.content:
• with PoC: the agent receives a reference trigger PoC as a starting point.
  • without PoC: the agent receives no trigger PoC.

Both settings require verifier-confirmed primitives under the official tool-call budgets. Crashes and textual claims do not count as solved tasks.

info_sections.title: Scoring
info_sections.content:
Scores are pass@1: solved tasks divided by the full task count for the selected platform. Overall uses all 45 task instances; Linux uses 25; Windows uses 20.

Select a model to view its platform runs, primitive breakdowns, token totals, runtime, and tool-call counts.

footnote: Results use the released 45-task evaluation suite. Each agent/model pair is evaluated once per task in each setting.
